newsitem.title: USA: Cephalon seeks FDA ok for narcolepsy drug.
newsitem.headline: Cephalon seeks FDA ok for narcolepsy drug.

text.p: Cephalon Inc said Tuesday that it has submitted a New Drug Application to the Food and Drug Administration to market modafinil, a drug sold in France to treat narcolepsy, in the United States.
The oral drug is sold in France for treating the sleep disorder, Cephalon said.

Cephalon said Laboratoire L. Lafon, the French pharmaceutical company that developed and sells modafinil, has given it exclusive rights to market the drug in the United States, Japan, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Mexico.
Narcolepsy is a chronic, lifelong sleep disorder that Cephalon said affects about 125,000 people in the United States. The most common symptom is excessive daytime sleepiness.
Cephalon said modafinil would be the first new drug to treat narcolepsy in the United States in more than 20 years if it is approved.

Cephalon said it conducted 14 clinical studies of the drug, including two multicenter Phase 3 trials involving 558 patients. In both studies the drug showed "a significant benefit in increasing patients' ability to stay awake and in improving their overall condition," Cephalon spokesman Jason Rubin said.
Cephalon is a biopharmaceutical company making and marketing treatments for neurological disorders.
